summary: The complete diff supports the saved claim. The sole production change retains a chunk-ending CR until its separator length is knowable. Independent public-API checks found no candidate mismatch across 32,956 checks; the same checker found 1,736 baseline mismatches. No functional compatibility regression was found within the stated scope.

Compatibility reasoning: the existing CRLF branch still consumes two characters, LF still consumes one, and CR followed by a non-LF still consumes one. Only a final-buffer CR is retained. The existing final flush appends LF, which consumes a retained final CR as one separator without losing its record. Retaining the whole unfinished record allows the existing quote rescan to preserve embedded newlines. Empty chunks leave the pending CR unchanged.

The observable timing tradeoff is that a standalone CR at the end of a chunk now delays that row and its callbacks until another chunk or EOF. The saved claim excludes callback timing guarantees; final rows, callback contents and single completion passed. This reviewer used Node 24 Web APIs, not an actual browser engine, and did not independently rerun full-suite/lint/docs acceptance or Node 22/20/25. Those broader acceptance obligations remain with the primary run evidence. This review does not establish split multibyte decoding, all malformed CSV diagnostics, universal CSV conformance, performance, or global novelty.
confirmed_scope: For the reviewed valid CSV inputs delivered as decoded strings or ASCII byte chunks, candidate e80bf7bb2f0716c5077e733a1eff89b1c63e7694 preserves CRLF as one record separator across stream boundaries, including intervening empty chunks, so nonzero header indexes and parsed rows match unsplit input. Independent checks cover Node streams, Node-hosted browser ReadableStreams and streamed File callbacks; real blank preamble records still count, standalone CR/LF and final CR work, and quoted newlines plus representative mapping/conversion options remain correct. The complete diff and checks support this localized separator-handling claim, without a claim of browser-engine coverage, callback timing equivalence, multibyte decoding, malformed-input correctness, performance or universal CSV compliance.
